 What Does Nicolas Cage Think of Ryan Gosling’s Ghost Rider Reboot? He Says…
 SYFY Follow Josh Weiss Add to Preferred Sources Updated Mon, November 9, 2026 at 4:04 PM UTC What Does Nicolas Cage Think of Ryan Gosling’s Ghost Rider Reboot? He Says… Nicolas Cage has officially given his blessing to the next Ghost Rider, Ryan Gosling .
 "Ryan's going to do his thing with it and I'm looking forward to seeing it," Cage told The Hollywood Reporte r at the Nov. 4 premiere of David O. Russell's Madden . "Ryan knows how I feel about him as an actor; we've had nice conversations and we stay in touch. I was happy for him and wished him best of luck on his adventures and I look forward to seeing the movie."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The National Treasure alum previously hopped aboard a flaming motorcycle as Marvel's Johnny Blaze in the 2007  Ghost Rider  movie written and directed by Mark Steven Johnson . Fittingly enough, the film starred Gosling's future wife, Eva Mendes. Cage returned four years later in Ghost Rider: Spirit of Vengeance  (directed by Mark Neveldine and Brian Taylor).
 "You get a chance to steward these characters for a couple years and then you got to step back and let other people do it," Steven Johnson predicted in  a 2024 interview with  SYFY Wire .  And as a fan, you're excited to see different interpretations. There's so many interpretations of Batman. I loved the new one and I can't wait to see where that goes. I would love to see different versions of Ghost Rider come along." 
 Gosling's Marvel Studios casting was announced at San Diego Comic-Con in July. The Oscar-nominated Barbie  actor will reunite with Star Wars: Starfighter writer/director duo Jonathan Tropper and Shawn Levy . Since Johnny Blaze and Robbie Reyes have already been depicted onscreen, there is every likelihood the reboot focuses on Johnny's brother, Danny Ketch.
 "We spent a lot of time last year making Starfighter and as Ryan started talking to me about his vision for this character and the opportunity and what this movie could be, we started riffing," Levy recalled at SDCC. "And finally, I was just like, 'Bro, let's ride.'"
 Advertisement Advertisement The filmmaker is no stranger to the MCU, having directed Deadpool & Wolverine , which became the highest-grossing R-rated movie of all time until it was deposed by Christopher Nolan's  The Odysey .
 Not much is known about the project, but  Bill Skarsgård  ( IT: Welcome to Derry ) and Connor Storrie  ( Heated Rivalry ) are rumored to star opposite Gosling, with Storrie reportedly playing the villain.
 When Does Ryan Gosling's  Ghost Rider  Movie Come Out?
 Marvel Studios'  Ghost Rider  is currently slated to hit theaters on June 28, 2028.
